recommended_media: independent SD card first; preserve eMMC untouched
backup_plan: record board serial/identity and WSL approval timestamp
read and hash current eMMC boot files BOOT.bin, boot.scr, system.dtb, uImage.lz4
capture current rootfs identity, /proc/cmdline, mounts, DTB semantics, CMA and module state
store backups outside Git with read-only permissions and a SHA256SUMS file
record serial console settings and a known-good eMMC boot path
candidate_sd_contents: BOOT.bin generated from the matched MLK HPF/bitstream/FSBL/U-Boot chain
matching system.dtb containing hard_npu, soft_npu and CMA/reserved-memory
matching driver modules or built-in configuration
Arm NN libraries, demo and model assets with a deployment manifest
write_and_boot_sequence: stop and obtain explicit human approval after all static and isolated-build gates pass
write only an independently identified SD device after a destructive-device confirmation
hash the written partitions and compare to the candidate manifest
boot with the board's documented SD selector and serial console attached
before loading modules, verify kernel, DTB, FPGA manager and CMA identities
verify module vermagic, symbol compatibility, compatible/reg/interrupt resources and dmesg
load order is vendor-confirmed only; candidate inference is cma_mem then hard_npu/soft_npu
verify /dev/cma_mem and the required NPU nodes before any demo
run at most one vendor-approved functional demo, not a benchmark
stop_conditions: board/device or package identity differs from the manifest
missing or unverified Module.symvers/symbol CRC compatibility
module probe failure, kernel warning, timeout or new device node mismatch
any request to modify eMMC, current rootfs, governor, kernel parameters or system libraries
rollback: remove the candidate SD and restore the documented eMMC boot selector
boot the previously hashed eMMC files
compare uname, cmdline, DTB hash, mount layout, CMA and module state to the backup record
if SD boot altered persistent configuration, stop and use serial recovery; do not overwrite eMMC automatically
